claims.text: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation can give a tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy ultrahigh strength at ambient and elevated temperatures.
The SCCP-enabled tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy has good tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
The SCCP-enabled tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy has good ductility at elevated temperatures.
Adding a lubricious secondary phase to an SCCP tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy will produce a self-lubricating material over a wide temperature range.
The lubricious-phase-modified alloy will retain the ultrahigh strength and ductility associated with the SCCP alloy architecture.
A sulfide or carbon-rich lubricious constituent can be incorporated into the alloy as coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates reinforce the tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy matrix.
The proposed nanoprecipitates form lubricious interfacial layers at grain boundaries or dislocation interfaces.
The coherent interfaces of SCCP nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission.
Dislocation transmission through the coherent nanoprecipitates preserves mechanical strength after incorporation of the lubricious phase.
Embedded lubricious phases provide low-shear-strength interfaces at high temperature.
The low-shear-strength interfaces reduce friction and wear under high-temperature sliding.
The modified composite will have a significantly lower friction coefficient over a broad temperature range.
The modified composite will have improved wear resistance over a broad temperature range.
The modified composite will retain at least 90% of the baseline mechanical strength.
Tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys without the proposed lubricious phase can possess high strength.
Tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys without the lubricious phase lack intrinsic self-lubrication and exhibit higher friction under extreme tribological conditions.
Above the lubricious phase's thermal-stability limit, diffusion or degradation may reduce lubrication efficiency.
